content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate interacts with numerous medications, primarily by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. These interactions can lead to increased drug levels, enhanced effects, or heightened toxicity of co-administered drugs. In some cases, erythromycin ethylsuccinate may also decrease the efficacy of certain medications. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Rimegepant: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rimegepant levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Alternative drugs should be considered. 2. Riociguat: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises riociguat levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Risperidone: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases risperidone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring or therapy modification. 4. Ritonavir: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ritonavir mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 5. Rivaroxaban: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate elevates rivaroxaban levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, especially in patients with renal impairment, as this may increase bleeding risk. 6. Roflumilast: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases roflumilast levels, potentially leading to adverse reactions. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 7. Romidepsin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises romidepsin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs should be used. 8. Rosuvastatin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rosuvastatin toxicity, likely through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Rucaparib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rucaparib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Ruxolitinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate elevates ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Sacubitril/Valsartan: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases valsartan levels, likely through hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1 inhibition. Close monitoring is required. 12. Saxagliptin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Selumetinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose and monitor closely. 14. Sertraline: Both sertraline and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 15. Sevoflurane: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, necessitating the use of alternative medications. 16. Sildenafil: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. A reduced starting dose of sildenafil (25 mg) is recommended. 17. Simvastatin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate significantly increases simvastatin levels, raising the risk of rhabdomyolysis. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Siponimod: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate elevates siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs should be used. 19. Sirolimus: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 20. Sodium Bicarbonate: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels are increased by sodium bicarbonate through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Similar to sodium bicarbonate, erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels are increased. Monitoring is necessary. 22. Sodium Picosulfate: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora. Alternative drugs should be considered. 23. Solifenacin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs are recommended. 24. Sonidegib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided. 25. Sorafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 26. Sotalol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 27. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 28. Stiripentol: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels are increased by stiripentol via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Sufentanil: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases sulbactam levels by inhibiting OATP1. Alternative drugs should be used. 31. Sunitinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs are recommended. 32. Suvorexant: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. A reduced starting dose of suvorexant (5 mg) is recommended. 33. Tacrolimus: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs should be used. 34. Tadalafil: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 35. Talazoparib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Tamoxifen: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases tamoxifen metabolism, potentially altering its efficacy. Monitoring is necessary. 37. Tamsulosin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose reduction may be required. 38. Tazemetostat: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided. 39. Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 40. Telavancin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 41. Temsirolimus: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 42. Tetrabenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 43. Tezacaftor: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose adjustment is recommended. 44. Theophylline: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 45. Thiamine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. Monitoring is necessary. 46. Thioridazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 47. Tinidazole: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Tipranavir: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 49. Tobramycin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tobramycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitoring is necessary. 50. Tofacitinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Dose adjustment may be required. 51. Tolterodine: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 52. Tolvaptan: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs should be used. 53. Topiramate: Topiramate decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via CYP3A4 induction. Alternative drugs are recommended. 54. Topotecan: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases topotecan levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided. 55. Toremifene: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases toremifene levels by reducing its metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so alternative drugs are recommended. 56. Trabectedin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitoring is necessary. 57. Tramadol: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome. Dose adjustment and monitoring are required. 58. Trazodone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 59. Triamcinolone Acetonide: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases triamcinolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. 60. Triazolam: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs should be used. 61. Trifluoperazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs are recommended. 62. Trimethoprim: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 63. Trimipramine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 64. Triptorelin: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases triptorelin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 65. Trofinetide: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels are increased by trofinetide via OATP inhibition. Alternative drugs should be used. 66. Tropisetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 67. Tucatinib: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels are increased by tucatinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided. 68. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine. Administration should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is complete. 69. Umeclidinium/Vilanterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs are recommended. 70. Valbenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 71. Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with this medication. Monitoring is necessary. 72. Valproic Acid: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases valproic acid levels by reducing its metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 73. Valsartan: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases valsartan levels, likely through OATP1B1 inhibition. Monitoring is necessary. 74. Vandetanib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs are recommended. 75. Vardenafil: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The vardenafil dose should be limited to 5 mg per 24 hours. 76. Vemurafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is not recommended. 77. Venetoclax: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases venetoclax levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Dose reduction and close monitoring are required. 78. Venlafaxine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are necessary. 79. Verapamil: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and verapamil mutually increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs are recommended. This list highlights the importance of careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or the use of alternative medications when erythromycin ethylsuccinate is co-administered with other drugs. Many interactions involve QTc prolongation, which can increase the risk of life-threatening arrhythmias.
